model: Life insurer FCFE at cost of equity, net debt held at zero (engine route)

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 IFRS 17 total revenue (insurance revenue + net investment result + fee income + other), SLF_Metrics.csv Revenue, C$ millions. Used only as the scale the margin is applied to: IFRS 17 revenue carries fair-value noise in the net investment result (FY2022 23.3bn, FY2023 40.8bn, FY2024 38.6bn, FY2025 41.9bn), so the growth_rates path is the growth of UNDERLYING NET INCOME the margin is calibrated to, not a forecast of the IFRS top line.
inputs.share_count_basis: 554.0M closing common shares at 30 June 2026 (Q2-2026 MD&A, section B Financial Summary and section I Capital table); the same 554M at 31 Dec 2025 (FY2025 MD&A line 'Closing common shares outstanding 554 / 574'). Dilutive convertibles add 0.01 to EPS (~0.5%), immaterial. The CSV's FY2025 SharesOutstanding of 564.6M is the weighted average for EPS, not the closing count. Held FLAT: SBC is charged in the flows and the NCIB (10M shares/yr authorised) is a use of the FCFE being capitalised, not extra growth.
inputs.net_debt_treatment: Held at ZERO. Total debt C$9,120M at 30 June 2026 = subordinated debentures 8,920 + innovative capital instruments 200 (Q2-2026 capital table). This is regulatory capital funding whose interest is inside underlying net income (Corporate segment), so the underlying-earnings flow is already post-financing; deducting the debt again would charge it twice. Consolidated cash C$14,788M is general-fund and policyholder liquidity, not surplus. SLF Inc. holdco cash and liquid assets of C$2.3bn (30 June 2026; C$2.4bn at 31 Dec 2025) are treated as the required holding-company buffer and NOT added to the bridge -- conservative by perhaps C$1bn (~C$1.8/share) if part of it is excess.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 organic FCFE estimate = 70% x underlying net income C$4,201M. Observed capital returned to common shareholders in FY2025 was C$3,771M (dividends 2,064 + buybacks 1,707) = 90% of underlying NI, but that was partly funded by C$2bn of new subordinated debt (financial leverage 20.1% -> 23.5%) and SLF Inc.'s LICAT then fell 157% -> 145% in H1-2026 on the C$2.4bn SLC Management affiliate buy-outs; FY2024 distributions were 73% and FY2023 55% of underlying NI, and C$6.9bn of M&A since 2020 was funded from retained capital. 70% is the organic conversion the three-year record supports. An insurer's OCF-less-capex (CSV FreeCashFlow 2,654) is not free cash, so the owner-FCF identity last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income is deliberately not satisfied.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Set equal to the FCFE proxy. The CSV's FY2025 FreeCashFlow of C$2,654M (OCF 2,799 - capex 145) is dominated by policyholder-liability and investment flows and is not a cash-generation measure for a life insurer.
inputs.sbc_source: SLF_Annual_FY2025.txt:14087 'Share-based payments (Note 18) 498 / 610' (cash-flow statement, C$ millions); FY2023 491, FY2022 227. SLF's plans are mostly cash-settled (DSUs, Sun Shares, PSUs) so the add-back is an accrual that is later paid in cash; it is already inside underlying net income. No separate net-share-settlement tax line (CSV EquityAwardTaxes 0). Charged at 1.19% of revenue; the street basis adds it back under the folder convention, but because the awards are cash-settled the house/street band overstates the real SBC sensitivity for this name.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 common shares purchased for cancellation C$1,707M (20.7M shares); FY2024 C$855M (11.5M shares); H1-2026 only C$83M (0.8M shares; Q1-2026 nil) because capital went to the SLC Management affiliate buy-outs and Bell Partners. The 2026 NCIB (up to 10M shares, 29 May 2026 - 28 May 2027) had bought 0.8M by 30 June 2026. Buyback pace is therefore well below FY2025 and the flat count is a modelling convention until it resumes.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in CAD; the NYSE quote is in USD. fx_rate is model -> quote: 1 CAD = 0.7019 USD (CAD=X 1.4247 USD/CAD, Yahoo Finance, 2026-10-04T04:21Z). Parity check: SLF.TO closed C$111.87 and NYSE SLF US$78.57 on 2026-10-02, implied 1.4238 USD/CAD vs 1.4247 spot (0.06% apart) -- the two listings are the same share. Unsuffixed intrinsic values are in USD to compare with current_price; the _cad twins are the model's native output. Two-thirds of underlying earnings are earned in USD and Asian currencies, so a weaker CAD raises the CAD earnings base while lowering the translation of CAD value into USD -- partially self-hedging at the per-share level.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-02T20:00:02Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API, NYSE); 52-week range 57.22-84.38
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of EQUITY 9.0% on CAD flows: Government of Canada 10-year ~3.4% + 5.5% ERP x beta ~1.0, rounded. Half to a full point below the 9.5-10.0% used for MET/PRU in USD because (a) the CAD risk-free rate is lower than the UST rate, (b) SLF has no legacy variable-annuity or guaranteed-universal-life run-off block, no governance failure in a major unit, and A+/AA/Aa3/AA operating-company ratings with LICAT 145% against a 100% supervisory ratio, and (c) a third of earnings is capital-light asset management and group benefits. It is a cost of equity, not a WACC, because the flows are post-interest FCFE. Same rate in all three scenarios; scenario risk sits in the driver paths and weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: lease liabilities C$924M (FY2025) are immaterial against C$425bn of assets and the lease cost is already inside the underlying expense base.
inputs.nci_treatment: Underlying net income is attributable to common shareholders -- after preferred-share dividends and distributions on other equity instruments (C$79M FY2025, C$80M FY2024) and after non-controlling interests (NCI equity C$199M at 30 June 2026, down from 264M after the BGO/Crescent minority buy-outs). Those two deductions are folded into the pre-tax margin rather than modelled as separate lines, a ~C$30M tax-shield distortion that is immaterial.
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE at cost of equity on a diversified life insurer / asset manager, run through the component engine with net debt at zero -- the PRU / MET / GL / IAG.AX cost-of-equity-stream precedent. The dcf-methods routing default for an insurer is BVPS-compounding x exit P/B; overridden because SLF does not compound book: it distributes ~75-90% of underlying earnings (dividends 47% payout plus buybacks), shareholders' equity has sat between C$22bn and C$27bn for a decade, IFRS 17 restated it from C$27.5bn (FY2022 IFRS 4) to C$23.6bn (FY2023), and BVPS moved only C$40.63 -> C$42.49 from FY2024 to June 2026 while underlying EPS grew 12%. The value driver is the distributable underlying earnings stream, not book growth. Using the same method as PRU/MET keeps the North American life insurers comparable. EARNINGS ANCHOR: underlying net income (management's non-IFRS measure, C$4,201M FY2025; TTM to June 2026 C$4,314M), not reported net income (C$3,551M FY2025, C$1,473M H1-2026), because reported income carries market-related impacts (interest-rate and real-estate marks), assumption changes, M&A integration and the C$145M Q1-2026 legal provision that are non-economic in any single year. The persistent gap (reported ran 68-85% of underlying over FY2023-25) is handled by calibrating FCFE conversion at 70% of underlying NI rather than treating all of underlying NI as distributable. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = FY2025 IFRS 17 total revenue C$41,900M; ebitda_margin_path = pre-tax underlying net income to common BEFORE share-based payments as % of revenue (FY2025: 4,201 / (1 - 0.195) + 498 = 5,717 -> 13.64%); sbc_pct_path 1.19%; da_pct_path 0 (no PP&E capex line for an insurer); cash_tax_rate_path 20.0% (FY2025 underlying effective rate 19.5%, H1-2026 20.0%, expected range 16-22%, Pillar Two adding 1-2pp), so (margin - SBC) x (1 - tax) = underlying net income to common; capex_pct_path = capital RETAINED in the insurance subsidiaries and holdco (new-business strain, LICAT and CSM growth, bolt-on M&A, the economic part of the reported-vs-underlying gap), set so FCFE = the scenario's conversion of underlying NI (base 70%, bull 75%, bear 62%); wc_capture 0. BVPS CROSS-CHECK: price C$111.87 = 2.63x BVPS C$42.49 against underlying ROE 18.7% (H1-2026) / 18.2% (FY2025) and a 20% medium-term target; at a 9% cost of equity and 3% growth the justified P/B is (18.7 - 3) / (9 - 3) = 2.6x, i.e. the market is already paying full justified value for the current ROE -- consistent with the DCF landing near the price. Underlying P/E 14.5x TTM. CAPITAL: SLF Inc. LICAT 145% (30 June 2026, from 157% at FY2025), Sun Life Assurance 133%; financial leverage 23.8% against a ~25% ceiling, so further debt-funded M&A or buybacks have little headroom and FY2026 distributions are running below FY2025 (H1-2026 buybacks C$83M vs C$918M).
inputs.fy2026_treatment: Year 1 = FY2026. H1-2026 underlying NI C$2,173M (+5.5% YoY; Q2 +11%), underlying EPS 3.90 (+8%), Q2 dividend raised to C$0.96 (C$3.84 run-rate). Base takes FY2026 underlying NI growth of 8% (~C$4.54bn): Q2 momentum, full attribution of BGO/Crescent earnings after the minority buy-outs, Bell Partners from July 2026, partly offset by the higher tax rate and Corporate interest on the C$2.75bn of new subordinated debt. The 10%+ medium-term underlying EPS objective includes ~2-3pp of buyback accretion that a flat-count FCFE model captures as distributed cash, not as growth.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: underlying_net_income_3yr_cagr (fcf_3yr_cagr above): FY2022 restated IFRS 17 C$3,369M -> FY2025 C$4,201M = 7.6%; cross-checked against underlying EPS 5yr 6.3% (FY2020 5.49 -> FY2025 7.45), underlying NI 5yr 5.5% (FY2020 3,213 -> 4,201), and the 10%+ EPS objective net of buyback accretion. Base year-1 at 8% then decelerating to 3%.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (~0% 5yr, -3.7% 3yr) diverges from EPS (8.4% / 5.7%) and underlying NI (5.5% / 7.6%) by far more than 30%. Expected for this name: SLF distributes most of its earnings and the IFRS 17 transition restated FY2022 equity from C$27.5bn to C$23.6bn, so book value is not the compounding base -- which is why the BVPS routing default is overridden. Revenue CAGRs are IFRS 17 artefacts (FY2022 revenue 23.3bn was the first IFRS 17 comparative) and are not used.
historical_growth.notes: fcf_* rows are UNDERLYING NET INCOME CAGRs, the flow this model capitalises; reported FCF (OCF - capex) is not meaningful for a life insurer (OCF swung -1,857 FY2021 to +5,612 FY2023 on policyholder flows). Reported EPS CAGRs use statutory EPS 4.10 (FY2020) / 5.21 (FY2022) / 6.15 (FY2025).

base.capex_rationale: capex_pct 2.99% of revenue = 30% of the 9.96% after-tax underlying margin retained -> FCFE conversion 70% of underlying NI, the organic level the FY2023-25 record supports once the debt-funded part of FY2025's 90% distribution is stripped out.
base.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 9% / 3% = 17.2x FCFE; capped at 16x FCFE = 11.2x underlying earnings at 70% conversion, inside SLF's 10-14x historical underlying P/E range. Cap binds.
base.narrative: Underlying NI grows 8% in FY2026 then decelerates to 3% by year 10: Asia compounds at low-double digits off Hong Kong in-force and bancassurance in India/Indonesia/Philippines, Canada grows mid-single digits, Sun Life Asset Management offsets MFS retail outflows with SLC alternatives (Crescent, BGO/Bell Partners) and the MFS active ETF build, and U.S. Dental stabilises without ever becoming a growth engine. Margin flat at the FY2025 level; underlying ROE drifts toward but does not reach the 20% target in the model's economics. 70% of underlying NI is distributable.

bull.capex_rationale: capex_pct 2.6% on a 10.4% after-tax margin = 25% retained -> 75% FCFE conversion, as capital-light asset management and group benefits grow faster than capital-heavy protection.
bull.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 9% / 3.5% = 18.8x FCFE; capped at 18x = 13.5x underlying earnings at 75% conversion -- the top of SLF's historical range, what the market pays for a 20%-ROE compounder.
bull.narrative: Management's medium-term objectives are met organically: 10%+ underlying NI growth for three years, underlying ROE through 20%. Asia's double-digit growth persists despite Hong Kong competition; the January 2026 Sun Life Asset Management combination lifts SLC alternatives fund-raising (record Crescent direct-lending and secondaries closes repeat) and MFS flows turn positive on the ETF range; Tony Mollica's U.S. Dental turnaround delivers a margin recovery from 2027; stop-loss and Health & Risk Solutions keep growing. Margin expands 55bp on operating leverage and mix; a higher share of earnings is capital-light so 75% converts to FCFE.

bear.capex_rationale: capex_pct 3.5% on a 9.1% after-tax margin = 38% retained -> 62% FCFE conversion, as LICAT is rebuilt from 145% and financial leverage is brought back from the 25% ceiling without the help of further debt issuance.
bear.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 9% / 2% = 14.6x FCFE; capped at 14x = 8.7x underlying earnings at 62% conversion -- a trough lifeco multiple.
bear.narrative: The bull's independent risks land together: U.S. Dental needs further impairments and Medicaid dental funding is cut, MFS outflows continue at tens of billions a year with fee compression, Hong Kong new-business CSM keeps falling under competitive pressure, and a 2027 equity-market and credit-spread drawdown cuts AUM fees and forces LICAT rebuilding -- so underlying NI growth is 3% / 1% / 2% before settling at 3%, 100bp of margin is lost, and with leverage at the 25% ceiling only 62% of underlying NI is distributable. The dividend is maintained but buybacks are suspended, as in H1-2026.

scenario_narratives.base: Underlying NI compounds 8% in FY2026 decelerating to 3% by year 10, margin flat at FY2025's level, 70% of underlying NI converted to FCFE; Asia and asset management carry growth, Canada is steady, U.S. Dental stabilises. Terminal 16x FCFE (11.2x earnings).
scenario_narratives.bull: Medium-term objectives met organically (10%+ growth, 20% ROE): Asia double-digit, SLC alternatives and the MFS ETF range turn asset-management flows, Dental turnaround delivers, margin +55bp, 75% FCFE conversion, terminal 18x FCFE.
scenario_narratives.bear: Dental impairments plus Medicaid cuts, persistent MFS outflows, Hong Kong margin compression and a 2027 market drawdown; growth 1-3%, margin -100bp, 62% conversion while LICAT and leverage are repaired, buybacks suspended; terminal 14x FCFE.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bull cut to 30% because it needs three independent things to go right at once -- the Dental turnaround, a reversal of MFS's multi-year outflows, and Asia sustaining double-digit growth while Hong Kong new-business margins are already compressing. Bear raised to 20% because several of its legs are live rather than hypothetical: financial leverage is at 23.8% against a ~25% ceiling, SLF Inc.'s LICAT has fallen 12 points in six months, H1-2026 buybacks have already collapsed to C$83M, and reported net income halved in Q1-2026 on rate marks and charges. No solvency or going-concern element, so the bear is not weighted higher than that.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Sun Life is valued as the distributable stream of underlying earnings a diversified life insurer and asset manager can pay its common shareholders, capitalised at a CAD cost of equity of 9%, with net debt held at zero because the subordinated debt is regulatory capital whose cost is already inside the earnings. Book value is a cross-check, not the model: at 2.6x BVPS on an 18.7% underlying ROE the market is already paying the justified P/B for the current return, so the opportunity, if any, rests on earnings growth above the ~7% the base assumes, not on re-rating.
key_risks_to_valuation: FCFE conversion: the 70% base is an estimate -- SLF does not disclose remittances or organic capital generation; FY2025's 90% distribution was partly debt-funded and H1-2026 shows the opposite (C$83M buybacks). Each 5pp of conversion is ~7% of value.
Cost of equity: a 1pp change in the 9% rate moves value ~12-15%; two-thirds of earnings are non-CAD, so a USD/Asian-currency cost of equity would be higher.

Underlying vs reported: reported net income has run 68-85% of underlying for three years; if the gap is partly economic (assumption changes, Dental impairments, legal provisions), the base overstates the distributable stream.
U.S. Dental and MFS flows are the two businesses that can turn the bear case on without any macro shock.
FX: the USD intrinsic value is a translation of a CAD value at 0.7019; a 5% CAD move shifts the USD IV 5% before any earnings offset.
Capital: LICAT 145% and 23.8% leverage leave little headroom for further debt-funded M&A; a market drawdown would be met by retaining more earnings, which is the bear's 62% conversion.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (NYSE: SLF, USD) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 57.22-84.38. TSX line SLF.TO used for the FX parity check only. CAD=X spot from the same API.
data_sources.financials: SLF_Metrics.csv (FY2014-Q2 2026, C$ millions, from the SEDAR annual reports and interim MD&As); underlying net income, underlying EPS, underlying tax rate, BVPS, LICAT, financial leverage, closing share count, NCIB and capital table from SLF_Annual_FY2025.txt, SLF_Annual_FY2024.txt, SLF_Annual_FY2023.txt, SLF_Annual_FY2022.txt, SLF_Annual_FY2021_MDA.txt and SLF_Quarterly_Q2-2026.txt.
data_sources.qualitative: SLF_Analysis.json (2026-10-04): segments, medium-term objectives (10%+ underlying EPS growth, 20% underlying ROE, 40-50% payout), Q1/Q2-2026 developments, bull and bear cases.
